event_text: The Bandaranaike Airport attack is carried out by 14 Tamil Tiger commandos, resulting in military and civilian casualties and destroyed aircraft.
story: The utter chaos that erupted at Bandaranaike Airport in 2001 was quite the spectacle, really. Susan, dear, I do believe I saw a chap's lunchbox go flying as a rather large explosion rocked the tarmac. Fourteen Tamil Tiger commandos, armed to the teeth, stormed the airport, because, well, that's just what one does on a Tuesday, I suppose. The military and civilian casualties were, of course, a frightful nuisance, and the destroyed aircraft were a bit of a blow to the local airline industry, but all in all, just another day in Sri Lanka, if you ask me. The Tigers, you see, were making a statement, and what better way to do so than by blowing up a few planes and murdering a handful of people? I mean, it's not as if it's going to make a lasting impact on the conflict or anything. The airport was, naturally, shut down for a bit, and the economy took a slight hit, but really, it's all just a minor blip on the radar of human history. Oh, and the commandos, well, they all died, because that's what tends to happen when one decides to take on the military in a rather... ill-advised manner.
regret_line: One might argue that a bit more thought should have been put into the whole "not getting killed" aspect of the plan.
winner_line: The international insurance industry, naturally, which saw a lovely spike in premiums and payouts thereafter.
